TITLE: A stair zone that holds part of a stair is measured from its drawn run
SOURCE: a multi-flight or winder stair is drawn flight by flight; one zone holds the run drawn in it
RATIONALE: M8: when the storey rise does not divide into the zone's drawn risers inside the 0.14 - 0.20 m band, the zone holds part of the stair. M4 kept it as a slab-zone exposure; the drawn run is now measured with the riser convention and the rest of the zone is landing. The storey-rise reading stays a diagnostic.

TITLE: Riser height of a drawn run whose riser the drawing does not fix
SOURCE: residential stair risers 150 - 180 mm
RATIONALE: Used only for a run whose storey rise does not give a riser inside the 0.14 - 0.20 m band, or a flight drawn outside any stair zone. A printed riser (profile STAIR_RISER_PRINTED_M or a note beside the flight) replaces it.

TITLE: A stair whose waist is not printed is priced at the usual waist
SOURCE: a QS prices a drawn stair at the usual waist and states the range
RATIONALE: M8: a stair measured from its drawn treads whose waist is not printed is PROVISIONAL (support CONVENTION_ONLY, confidence LOW) with STAIR_WAIST_CONVENTION_M, instead of UNRESOLVED with the waist range as exposure. UNRESOLVED_EXPOSURE keeps the M4 behaviour.

TITLE: Stair waist when no section prints it (priced)
SOURCE: villa stair waists 15 - 20 cm
RATIONALE: The same range as STAIR_WAIST_EXPOSURE_M, used as a stated convention for a PROVISIONAL stair.

TITLE: A flight drawn at the same place on two vertically adjacent plans
SOURCE: the ground-beam plan and the slab plan above it both draw the flight that rises between them
RATIONALE: Measured once (the drawing with more treads); the second drawing's own volume is an exposure 0 .. v, so the stacked-flights reading stays inside the bounded range.

TITLE: Tread directions are compared modulo 180 degrees
SOURCE: a line and the same line drawn the other way are one direction
RATIONALE: M8 metamorphic harness: a horizontal tread at 179.99 degrees (a drawing rotated by 180 degrees, floating noise) fell in another direction bin than one at 0 degrees, the flight split and the stair zone was read differently. Directions are now binned modulo 180 degrees.

TITLE: Tread lines of a settled stair family outside any stair zone
SOURCE: a flight is drawn as parallel tread lines at a tread pitch
RATIONALE: M8: measured as a flight (risers = lines + 1, convention riser, waist) with no landing (none is drawn); an unsettled family stays an exposure.

TITLE: Completeness findings become measured items or bounded exposures
SOURCE: a QS prices every drawn element and lists what is not drawn as an allowance
RATIONALE: M8 (engine.source.scope_quantities): a finding whose family is settled (one family, shape and words agree, confidence MEDIUM or HIGH) and whose plan geometry is enough is measured PROVISIONAL from the drawn geometry with the conventions below for what the drawing does not print; every other finding gets an exposure range by its kind and shape. Nothing stays volume-less; a finding never adds twice.

TITLE: A drawn group on a non-structural layer is not concrete
SOURCE: furniture, fixtures, services and landscape layers on a plan (FURN, FIXTURE, EQUIP, SANITARY, PLUMB, ELEC, LIGHT, HVAC, MECH, LANDSCAPE, TREE, PLANTING, IRRIGATION, INTERIOR, DECOR, CARPET, TILE, FLOORING, CEILING)
RATIONALE: M8 metamorphic harness: rectangles and circles on a furniture layer became pits, domes and bounded drawn-not-measured groups. A group whose layer name carries one of these words is a qualifier (0 .. 0), never measured and never bounded.

TITLE: Dimension notes beside a drawn element are its printed values
SOURCE: DEPTH / HEIGHT / H= / THK / T= / WAIST / RISER notes written beside the element
RATIONALE: A note within 1.5 m of the element's outline, keyword then number (mm when >= 20, else m; CM when written), replaces the convention for that dimension and is recorded on the item.

TITLE: Pool wall height, floor top to coping, when not printed
SOURCE: residential pools: water depth 1.2 - 1.8 m plus freeboard
RATIONALE: Walls = drawn wall plan area (ring, or strip length x drawn thickness) x this height.

TITLE: Pool wall thickness when the plan draws a single outline
SOURCE: RC pool walls 200 - 300 mm
RATIONALE: Used only when no double outline gives the wall thickness.

TITLE: Pool floor slab thickness when not printed
SOURCE: RC pool floors 200 - 300 mm
RATIONALE: Floor = the pool's outer plan area x this thickness.

TITLE: Lift / sump pit wall height when not printed
SOURCE: residential lift pits 1.0 - 1.5 m below the lowest landing
RATIONALE: Walls = drawn wall plan area x this height.

TITLE: Pit wall thickness when the plan draws a single outline
SOURCE: pit walls 200 - 250 mm
RATIONALE: Used only when no double outline gives it.

TITLE: Pit base slab thickness when not printed
SOURCE: pit bases 200 - 300 mm
RATIONALE: Not added when the pit lies inside a measured footing (the footing is its base).

TITLE: RC water tank wall height when not printed
SOURCE: villa roof / ground RC tanks 1.2 - 2.0 m high
RATIONALE: Walls = drawn wall plan area x this height.

TITLE: Tank wall thickness when the plan draws a single outline
SOURCE: RC tank walls 150 - 250 mm
RATIONALE: Used only when no double outline gives it.

TITLE: Tank cover (and base) slab thickness when not printed
SOURCE: RC tank slabs 150 - 250 mm
RATIONALE: A tank drawn on a slab plan stands on that measured slab: the cover slab only; elsewhere base and cover.

TITLE: Plan side of a tank that is named but not drawn (exposure only)
SOURCE: villa RC tanks 1.5 - 2.5 m square
RATIONALE: A tank referenced in notes with no drawing is an allowance: exposure 0 (a GRP tank on plinths) .. the RC tank of this side, TANK_HEIGHT_M high and the high thicknesses.

TITLE: A radial or ring group on the topmost slab plan is a dome when the set names domes
SOURCE: dome ribs and dome rings are drawn on the roof plan; a stair needs a storey above it to arrive at
RATIONALE: On the topmost slab plan, lines radiating from a circle centre (or two concentric circles) with a DOMES word anywhere in the set are a dome (PROVISIONAL, LOW); below the top plan, or with no dome word, the group stays an exposure under each candidate family.

TITLE: Dome rise over its base radius when no section prints it
SOURCE: villa domes are hemispherical (1.0) or shallower (0.5)
RATIONALE: Spherical cap: shell area pi (r^2 + h^2), h = ratio x r, r = the drawn radius.

TITLE: Dome shell thickness when not printed
SOURCE: RC dome shells 100 - 150 mm
RATIONALE: Shell volume = cap area x thickness.

TITLE: Depth of a dome ring drawn as two circles and not measured as a beam
SOURCE: dome ring beams 300 - 600 mm deep
RATIONALE: Ring = the drawn ring area x this depth; a ring already measured as a curved beam band is not added.

TITLE: Radius of a dome that is named but not drawn (exposure only)
SOURCE: villa domes 2 - 5 m across
RATIONALE: Allowance 0 .. the cap of this radius at the high rise and shell.

TITLE: Inner side of a lift pit that is named but not drawn (exposure only)
SOURCE: residential lift pits 1.5 - 2.2 m square
RATIONALE: Allowance 0 .. walls and base of this pit at the high depth.

TITLE: Plan area of a pool that is named but not drawn (exposure only)
SOURCE: villa pools 12 - 40 m2
RATIONALE: Allowance 0 .. walls and floor of a square pool of this area.

TITLE: One small RC element named but not drawn, or with no rule (exposure only)
SOURCE: a ramp, planter, wall piece or cantilever portion of a villa
RATIONALE: Allowance 0 .. high for a family with no geometry rule; never in the measured total.

TITLE: Roof parapet height when not printed (exposure only)
SOURCE: roof parapets 0.9 - 1.2 m
RATIONALE: Exposure 0 (a block parapet) .. free roof edge x this height x thickness.

TITLE: Roof parapet thickness when not printed (exposure only)
SOURCE: parapets 150 - 250 mm
RATIONALE: See PARAPET_HEIGHT_M.

TITLE: A boundary-wall strip takes the section of the family's schedule row of its width
SOURCE: a schedule row keyed by the family's mark ('B.W') printing the drawn width as its first size
RATIONALE: PROVISIONAL strip length x the row's width x its second size; no row of the drawn width: exposure with BOUNDARY_WALL_RC_SECTION_M2.

TITLE: RC section of a boundary-wall foundation per metre when no row binds
SOURCE: a 0.2 x 0.4 - 0.6 tie beam with or without a strip footing
RATIONALE: Exposure only: 0 .. strip length x the high section.

TITLE: Drop of a sunken slab outline when not printed (exposure only)
SOURCE: sunken wet areas 50 - 400 mm
RATIONALE: A sunken outline inside a measured panel adds its edge: perimeter x drop x the panel thickness (0 .. high).

TITLE: Depth that bounds an unidentified drawn strip (exposure only)
SOURCE: a strip on a structural plan could be a beam or wall of up to this depth
RATIONALE: Exposure 0 .. strip length x drawn width x the high depth.

TITLE: Section that bounds unidentified linework per metre (exposure only)
SOURCE: a pair of drawn lines could be a member of up to 0.4 x 0.4
RATIONALE: Exposure 0 .. half the linework length x the high section.

TITLE: Every finding without a volume gets a range by its kind and shape
SOURCE: engine.source.scope_quantities.BOUND_RULES
RATIONALE: Regions held for a detail: 0 .. area x the high slab thickness; a referenced family with no drawing: its allowance; a footing / beam row on no plan: one instance (beam: the longest measured span); a column drawn without an item: its own volume; an item with no presence: -its volume .. 0; a fill on a measured member: -area x the member's thickness .. 0 (a void); a member overlap: -overlap x depth .. 0; a note on a measured member: a qualifier with no volume of its own (0 .. 0, stated); a missing storey plan: the neighbouring storeys' measured slab + beam volume.

TITLE: A storey named by a height or a schedule band but with no plan
SOURCE: storeys of one villa carry similar slab and beam volumes
RATIONALE: Exposure = min .. max of the neighbouring storeys' measured slab + beam volume (one neighbour: 0.5 .. 1.0 of it).
